evals.prompt: /tw:style-check docs/ — we don't have a style guide.
evals.expected_output: Should ask once whether a style guide or terminology list exists outside the repo before concluding there isn't one. Only then should it run in derive mode: apply tw:docs-standards as the default for what it settles (sentence-case headings, 'you', present tense) and treat drift from it as findings even if most pages break it, derive the remaining conventions from the majority with counts, flag even splits as open decisions, and propose the terminology list the project is missing. Should write _reports/docs-style-check.md and never edit a page.
expectations: Asks whether a guide exists elsewhere before deriving
Applies docs-standards defaults as findings even against a majority
Derives other conventions from the majority with counts
Flags even splits as open decisions with a recommendation
Proposes missing terminology entries
Writes the report to _reports/docs-style-check.md without editing pages
Records the scope, version, exclusions and standard in the report header

evals.prompt: Sweep our docs: I think we call the same thing 'workspace', 'project' and 'space' in different places.
evals.expected_output: Should sweep the whole set, not a sample, cluster the variants, count each with locations, check which term the product's UI and API use, name the likely winner, and propose a terminology entry with the variants under 'don't use'. Should check the places drift hides — titles, navigation labels, headings, table cells, captions, link text, frontmatter and code comments — and also check whether one of the words is doing two jobs.
expectations: Sweeps the whole set, not a sample
Counts every variant with locations
Checks the UI and API for the product's own term
Proposes a terminology entry with don't-use variants
Checks titles, navigation, tables, captions and link text
Checks whether a word names two concepts
Asks which docs to sweep, since no path is given, before sweeping

evals.prompt: Our style guide says navigation labels are title case. Run the style check on docs/.
evals.expected_output: Should treat title-case navigation labels as the project's recorded decision, not drift, and flag navigation labels that break it. Should apply docs-standards defaults only where the guide is silent, and report drift against the guide with counts.
expectations: Uses the project's guide as the standard
Does not flag title-case navigation labels as drift
Flags labels that break the guide's rule
Applies docs-standards only where the guide is silent

evals.prompt: We fixed a bunch of terminology last month. Run the style check again and just confirm those are still fixed.
evals.expected_output: Should run a complete fresh sweep rather than only re-checking earlier findings, since an earlier report isn't evidence of today's state. Should read the previous report for its scores only, number findings from 1, overwrite the report, and show the score trend against the previous run.
expectations: Runs a complete fresh sweep
Does not treat the earlier report as evidence
Reads only the previous scores for the trend
Numbers findings from 1 and overwrites the report
